configurePresets.name: core
configurePresets.description: Shared configuration for every platform/compiler preset. NOTE: VCPKG_CHAINLOAD_TOOLCHAIN_FILE is the single source of truth for the chainloaded compiler toolchain and is set per concrete preset; the vcpkg overlay triplets must NOT also set it.

configurePresets.name: windows-msvc
configurePresets.description: Windows/MSVC toolchain selection, shared by the Release and Debug presets. The compiler is pinned through the chainloaded toolchain rather than left to PATH: cl.exe is not on PATH outside a Developer PowerShell, so an unpinned Ninja configure resolves to whatever else is there (clang) and builds something nobody asked for. The toolchain imports the MSVC environment itself, so these presets configure from any shell.

configurePresets.name: windows-msvc-arm64
configurePresets.description: Windows/MSVC toolchain selection, arm64 target (roadmap DR8, GitHub's hosted windows-11-arm runner). Same chainloaded toolchain file as windows-msvc - cmake/toolchains/windows.msvc.toolchain.cmake resolves the target-appropriate MSVC tools subdirectory from AC3_MSVC_TARGET_ARCH the same way linux.gcc.toolchain.cmake/macos.llvm.toolchain.cmake already resolve their own arm64 legs from VCPKG_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE - only the vcpkg triplet differs. AC3FORGE_BUILD_GUI is OFF here, unlike windows-msvc: not because ac3gui cannot be built for arm64, but because at authoring time Qt's only Windows arm64 kit for the pinned 6.8.3 (win64_msvc2022_arm64_cross_compiled) is a cross-compile kit expecting a paired win64_msvc2022_64 install for its host tools, and aqtinstall has a documented CI bug against exactly that combination - real complexity this leg's native-arm64-host build doesn't need to take on for a first pass. The same 'Qt kit not assumed present' shape linux-gcc/linux-llvm/macos-llvm already use, not a new pattern - see those presets' own descriptions and docs/platforms/windows.md's ARM64 section.

configurePresets.name: windows-llvm
configurePresets.description: Windows/clang-cl toolchain selection. clang-cl is MSVC-ABI compatible, so it links the same vcpkg packages and the same prebuilt msvc2022_64 Qt kit as the MSVC presets.

configurePresets.name: linux-gcc
configurePresets.description: Linux/GCC 16 toolchain selection. The GUI is off because a Qt kit is not assumed present, NOT because it cannot be built: cmake/FindQt6.cmake resolves Linux kits fine (distro packages land on CMake's own prefixes, and relocated / aqtinstall kits are searched under ~/Qt, /opt/Qt and friends), and ac3gui builds under both Linux presets and passes its headless --smoke run against Ubuntu 26.04's Qt 6.10. Add -DAC3FORGE_BUILD_GUI=ON on a machine that has Qt 6.5+; a preset that cannot find Qt should still say so by not asking for it rather than by failing to configure.

configurePresets.name: linux-llvm
configurePresets.description: Linux/LLVM 22 toolchain selection. GUI off for the same reason as linux-gcc.

configurePresets.name: linux-gcc-arm64
configurePresets.description: Linux/GCC 16 toolchain selection, arm64 (Raspberry Pi 4/5 and any other aarch64 Debian/Ubuntu target). Same toolchain file as linux-gcc - cmake/toolchains/linux.gcc.toolchain.cmake already resolves aarch64 vs x86_64 from VCPKG_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE - only the vcpkg triplet differs. GUI off for the same reason as linux-gcc.

configurePresets.name: linux-llvm-arm64
configurePresets.description: Linux/LLVM 22 toolchain selection, arm64 (Raspberry Pi 4/5 and any other aarch64 Debian/Ubuntu target). Same toolchain file as linux-llvm - cmake/toolchains/linux.llvm.toolchain.cmake already resolves aarch64 vs x86_64 from VCPKG_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE - only the vcpkg triplet differs. GUI off for the same reason as linux-gcc.

configurePresets.name: macos-llvm
configurePresets.description: macOS (Apple Silicon)/Homebrew LLVM toolchain selection. Verified via CI only (this project has no local macOS host) - see docs/building.md's Verified configuration section. GUI off by default for the same reason as linux-gcc - not because it cannot be built, but because a Qt kit is not assumed present on every Mac. CI's macos-llvm leg installs Homebrew's qt formula and passes -DAC3FORGE_BUILD_GUI=ON, the same opt-in shape as the four Linux build legs.

configurePresets.name: macos-llvm-x64
configurePresets.description: macOS (Intel)/Homebrew LLVM toolchain selection, x86_64. Same toolchain file and reasoning as macos-llvm - cmake/toolchains/macos.llvm.toolchain.cmake already resolves x64 vs arm64 from VCPKG_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE, falling back to uname -m outside a vcpkg port-build context - only the vcpkg triplet differs, same shape as linux-gcc-arm64 next to linux-gcc. Verified via CI only, on GitHub's macos-15-intel runner (real native Intel hardware, not Rosetta emulation - see .github/workflows/_build.yml's matrix entry). GUI off by default for the same reason as macos-llvm.

configurePresets.name: wasm-emscripten
configurePresets.description: Emscripten/WASM toolchain selection for the roadmap-F3 browser decode demo. Unlike every other platform preset here, this does NOT inherit "core": there is no host-OS condition (Emscripten cross-compiles from any host with $EMSDK set) and, more importantly, no vcpkg toolchainFile - see cmake/toolchains/wasm.emscripten.toolchain.cmake's own header for why going through vcpkg's community wasm32-emscripten triplet would be pure cost for zero benefit here. Everything "core" would otherwise supply (Ninja generator, binaryDir, the default ON options) is set directly below instead, deliberately turning off everything this preset does not need (CLI/GUI/tests/live-audio-linking containers) rather than inheriting defaults meant for a full desktop build.

configurePresets.name: sanitize-asan-ubsan
configurePresets.description: AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, fatal on first violation (-fno-sanitize-recover=all in cmake/Sanitizers.cmake) rather than logging and continuing. Deliberately does NOT add -fsanitize=integer's unsigned-integer-overflow check: this codec relies on intentional unsigned wraparound (CRC16, ring-buffer indices, the splice counter), and blanket-enabling it drowns real findings in expected wraparound. Signed overflow and out-of-range shifts - the precedent bug's own category (commit 8386c8f) - are already part of the default 'undefined' set.

configurePresets.name: sanitize-tsan
configurePresets.description: ThreadSanitizer. A SEPARATE preset from sanitize-asan-ubsan rather than more entries in its list, because the two runtimes are mutually exclusive - clang refuses -fsanitize=address,thread outright - and because they answer different questions: ASan/UBSan ask whether a single thread's memory and arithmetic are sound, TSan asks whether two threads agree on who owns what. Nothing in the ASan+UBSan leg can see a data race, which is the whole reason this exists (roadmap VX16): src/audio is a lock-free SPSC ring, a silence watchdog and a clock-drift servo shared between a real-time callback thread and the encoder thread, and a missing acquire/release there is invisible to every other gate in this repository. cmake/Sanitizers.cmake already took an arbitrary comma-separated list, so this preset adds no build-system machinery of its own.

configurePresets.name: coverage
configurePresets.description: gcov source coverage instrumentation (cmake/Coverage.cmake) over every library component - ac3::forge, ac3::audio, ac3::signing, matroska/mp4/mpegts, the C API, and (via AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM=ON plus vcpkg's 'adm' feature, the same pair ci.yml's adm-validate job passes) ac3adm/admbridge - plus ac3cli and ac3tests. AC3FORGE_BUILD_CLI is ON here (roadmap VX15): apps/cli is ~6,500 lines that front every other CI gate, tests/cli/test_cli.cpp runs the real built binary as a subprocess, and tools/checks/coverage_report.sh now gates it alongside the library components, so leaving it out meant the most-exercised executable in the tree had no floor at all. Examples stay off - they are documentation that happens to compile, tests/ already covers the same API surface, and each one is its own ctest process. AC3FORGE_BUILD_GUI stays off too: the GUI needs a Qt kit no Linux CI leg installs (see coverage_report.sh's own note).

configurePresets.name: minimal-decoder
configurePresets.description: Roadmap PF7's minimum-footprint decoder profile: ONE decode-only static library (ac3::forge_minimal) plus apps/baremetal's probe, built without exceptions, without RTTI and without the direct-form transform tables. Every other component is off - not as a time saving but because the root CMakeLists.txt refuses the combination: nothing under apps/, tests/, examples/ or the container modules builds against a decode-only archive. See cmake/MinimalDecoder.cmake and docs/building.md.

configurePresets.name: shared-libs
configurePresets.description: BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON, proving ac3::forge_shared/matroska::matroska_shared actually work - not just that the CMake topology configures, but that every in-tree consumer (ac3cli/ac3gui/ac3tests/examples) links and runs against the real .so, including the one example that also needs matroska's .so alongside ac3forge's. See .github/workflows/_build.yml's 'Configure, build and test with BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON' step, which runs this as an extra pass inside the existing linux-llvm leg rather than a new matrix entry - the same shape as the alsa_fallback step below it.

configurePresets.name: config-windows-llvm-coverage
configurePresets.description: The Windows counterpart of config-linux-gcc-coverage, for the code that only builds here: the Desktop Atmos Demo (apps/windows, docs/platforms/windows-demo.md) and the GUI. clang-cl's -fprofile-instr-generate/-fcoverage-mapping rather than gcov, read with tools/checks/coverage_windemo.ps1, which is how the demo gets line AND branch figures. Inherits the RELEASE base, not debug, on purpose: LLVM ships clang_rt.profile against the release CRT, and an instrumented /MDd binary runs to completion and then dies in the profile writer at exit (access violation, no profile written); cmake/Coverage.cmake's clang-cl arm turns optimisation off again (/Od /Ob0) so line and branch attribution stays exact. ADM stays off: vcpkg's adm feature is a Linux-leg concern and this preset exists for apps/windows.

configurePresets.name: config-arm-none-eabi-minimal
configurePresets.description: arm-none-eabi (Cortex-M3, no OS) cross build of the minimum-footprint decoder profile - the concrete target roadmap PF7 names, run under QEMU's mps2-an385 machine by tools/checks/run_baremetal_probe.sh. Like the Emscripten preset and for the same reasons, this does NOT inherit "core": there is no vcpkg triplet for bare-metal arm and nothing this profile builds has a third-party dependency, so the generator, binaryDir and options are set here directly rather than inherited from a preset meant for a hosted build.
